symptom: Mobile event pages regressed to short wide card images, oversized vertical bands, separated guide headings and controls, and a dense two-column footer.
expected_behavior: Every place-card rail uses the approved vacation 4:3 media proportion, event sections use compact spacing, and the mobile footer is grouped and readable without losing any link.
environment: Exact locally built VII candidate served by scripts/preview-built-candidate.mjs on port 4191 at 390x844 and 1440x1000.
authorization_boundary: The request authorizes local repair and verification; this candidate is saved but is not published without a separate publication instruction.

steps: Open the production events page at a 390 pixel mobile viewport.
Measure an event rail image and the direct event section padding.
Scroll to the guide section and the mobile footer.
Compare the same surfaces with the vacation card and the attached PDF.
reproduction.evidence: Before repair, event rail media measured 339x183 at ratio 1.85, direct event sections computed to 48px vertical padding, and the mobile footer measured about 1465px high.

observations.observation: A late generic mobile section rule overrode the compact event-world rhythm.
observations.evidence: Computed styles on production showed 48px top and bottom padding despite event-specific styles declaring 18px and 26px.

observations.observation: The horizontal card stylesheet explicitly assigned a 1.85 media aspect ratio.
observations.evidence: app/slider-card-compact.css contained the 1.85 ratio for event, spa, stay and discovery place-card rails instead of the vacation 4:3 contract.

observations.observation: Generic mobile footer and section-head rules caused both layout regressions.
observations.evidence: app/mobile-polish.css forced the first section-head child to a full row and forced footer navigation into dense two-column grids.

hypotheses.mechanism: Later generic mobile selectors won the cascade over event-world spacing and footer layout rules.
hypotheses.prediction: Stronger world-scoped selectors and a dedicated mobile footer structure will immediately reduce measured section and footer heights.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Apply only the scoped cascade repair, rebuild, and compare computed padding and footer geometry at 390 pixels.
hypotheses.result: Supported: event section padding became 18 to 24px and the footer decreased from about 1465px to 642px without removing links.

hypotheses.mechanism: Invisible deferred components or loading placeholders reserve the blank vertical space.
hypotheses.prediction: The empty bands will remain after CSS specificity changes because their height comes from hidden DOM placeholders.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Inspect visible DOM geometry and recompute page height after changing only section and footer CSS.
hypotheses.result: Rejected: the bands collapsed after the CSS-only repair and no hidden placeholder accounted for the prior measured padding.

hypotheses.mechanism: A shared compact rail stylesheet encoded 1.85 and overrode the approved vacation 4:3 place-card media shape.
hypotheses.prediction: Replacing the encoded ratio with one shared 4:3 token will align all four place-card worlds.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Measure the first place-card image on vacations, spas, hourly and events after the rebuilt candidate loads.
hypotheses.result: Supported: all four routes measured 339x254.25 with a ratio of 1.33 at 390 pixels.

affected_family: Event landing sections and editorial guide controls on mobile
Vacation, event, spa and hourly horizontal place-card media
Shared site footer on mobile and desktop breakpoints
Responsive transitions between compact mobile groups and desktop link columns

fix.change: Introduced one 4:3 place-card media token, added higher-specificity compact event spacing, and replaced the mobile footer link dump with three accessible disclosure groups while retaining normal desktop columns.
fix.evidence: The exact rebuilt candidate has no horizontal overflow, event sections compute to 18 to 24px padding, all four world cards measure 4:3, and footer links remain visible on desktop and expandable on mobile.

regression_checks.check: Exact candidate production build completes successfully
regression_checks.evidence: pnpm build exited with code 0 and completed all five vinext stages plus asset and startup-budget verification.
At 390x844, /search, /spas, /hourly and /events each measured 339x254.25 and ratio 1.33.

regression_checks.check: Mobile event spacing and horizontal overflow
regression_checks.evidence: Event sections measured 18 to 24px vertical padding and document scroll width did not exceed the 390px viewport.

regression_checks.check: Mobile footer disclosure behavior and content retention
regression_checks.evidence: Three groups rendered closed by default; opening the first set aria-expanded=true and displayed six links in a 264px grid.
